what_happened: Re-verification found that leanprover/lean-action@v1 (used by all three CI workflows) already implements a built-in actions/cache restore/save around the whole .lake directory (default use-github-cache: true), so .lake/build for FormalSystem/Mathlib is already cached across CI runs -- confirmed live via gh run log and gh api .../actions/caches (4 live ~2.6GB cache entries). The task's filed deliverable (a) (add a new actions/cache step scoped to .lake/build) would duplicate this existing mechanism; recommended NOT implementing it as filed. Deliverable (b) (timeout-minutes parity) stands unaffected.

Carried-figure re-validation at plan time found the description's scale figures drifted upward since filing (2026-11-02): FormalSystem modules 716 -> 772, lines 371,441 -> 416,312, .lake/build 6.3 GB -> 6.4 GB; matrix-seam figures also drifted (Metalogic/Decidability 179/106,266 -> 186/127,509; Metalogic/Expressiveness 143/104,211 -> 157/111,856). Direction of drift strengthens rather than weakens the task's motivation, so no plan change followed; figures restated live in the plan rather than copied.

The research report's Context Extension Recommendation asserts docs/development/CI_CD_PROCESS.md 'does not currently document' lean-action's default-on GitHub Actions cache. Checked live: the file already carries a '### GitHub Actions Cache' section (line 366) stating the primary/fallback key shape and the use-github-cache: false disable switch. The genuine gap is narrower -- the per-job cache-save boundary (snapshot taken inside the lean-action step, so later lake build steps in the same job are uncovered) and the live-verification pointer. Plan phase 2 amends the existing section rather than adding a new one.

Research's live-evidence reversal of deliverable (a) (lean-action@v1 already caches .lake by default; 4 live cache entries; restore visible in a run log) made the plan materially smaller and cheaper than the filing implied: one functional line in ci.yml instead of a new cache lifecycle. Reversal was stated plainly in the report's Executive Summary and Decisions, which is why it was impossible to miss at plan time.

validate-artifact.sh's Tier Justification measurement check caught a false __FULL_SWEEP__ sentinel claim in phase 1 before the plan was accepted. Root cause: suite_selection_select was first run with all three candidate paths at once, where the markdown path's __FULL_SWEEP__ dominated the combined result and masked that .github/workflows/ci.yml alone resolves to test-lint-roadmap-batch-proposals.sh and lakefile.toml alone resolves to six real suites. Fix: resolve the selector PER PHASE over that phase's own Files to modify set, never over a union of candidate paths. Both Tier Justification lines were rewritten to name verify-touched.sh with the phase's own paths; the validator then passed with 0 warnings.

verify-touched.sh (both bare and scoped to .github/workflows/ci.yml) exits 2 at preflight on a pre-existing, unrelated defect: .claude/scripts/tests/suite-selection-map.data line 37 names test-verification-scope-lib.sh, which does not exist yet (a self-referential new-library suite not yet landed, per the data file's own comment). This finding names no file in this task's scope (ci.yml, lakefile.toml, CI_CD_PROCESS.md); treated per the dispatch's baseline-delta rule as a pre-existing recorded PASS for Phase 1, not a block. No edit was made to suite-selection-map.data or verification-scope-lib.sh -- out of this task's file scope.

Phase 2's documentation amendment to docs/development/CI_CD_PROCESS.md (GitHub Actions Cache subsection) and the lakefile.toml lean_exe-count comment fix both passed readme-lint.sh (0 broken references, 0 missing READMEs) and stayed inside prose/comment regions confirmed by git diff read-through (tomllib parse of declared targets unchanged before/after).
